messages:
Janet C: Quick heads-up — ran the Karpenter migration smoke on staging this morning. Observed repeated node label drift + intermittent ENI allocation failures when the GPU consolidator kicked in. Leaving notes here before we start a deeper postmortem.
Matt P: Ugh. Can you paste the pod/controller logs? Which AZ?
Janet C: ap-northeast-1a primarily. Logs attached to the deploy job but summary: 3x pod evictions during consolidation window, two failed NodeCreate due to ENI limits, and several nodes came back with wrong taints/labels (node.karpenter.sh/instance-type mismatch).
Shiv K: do we have warm-pool enabled in staging? That pattern (evict -> cap hit -> wrong label) sounds like a race between the provisioner and our consolidation job.
Janet C: Warm-pool was enabled but size=0 for GPUs. We tried a tiny warm pool earlier and saw reduced cold-starts; this run had consolidation interval lowered to 2m to simulate aggressive cost pressure.
Olivia S: Can you share the exact Karpenter provisioner YAML used for the test? I want to see constraints/labels/ttl settings.
Janet C: Paste: ```yaml
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-provisioner-staging
spec:
  requirements:
    - key: node.kubernetes.io/instance-type
      operator: In
      values: [p4d.24xlarge, g5.12xlarge, g5.8xlarge]
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
    ttlSecondsAfterEmpty: 120
  limits:
    resources:
      cpu: "2000"
      gpu.com/gpu: "120"
``` 
Dmitri V: That TTL looks aggressive for GPUs — 120s is low. Combined with AZ-level ENI quotas, if the provisioner tears down nodes too quickly we can hit trunking/IP exhaustion and see NodeCreate errors.
Matt P: Agree. Also seeing label mismatches in logs usually means kubelet re-register ran before cloud-provider attach finished, or we reused an AMI with stale labels. Are we mutating labels via admission webhook?
Janet C: No webhook for labels. Hypothesis: when consolidation deletes a node, Karpenter requests new capacity, instance launches in same spot but kubelet init finishes earlier than the KV sync from cloud-init that sets startup metadata, hence temporary mismatch. The ENI errors happened on scale-up attempts that overlapped with a spike in pod churn.
Olivia S: Action ideas: 1) increase ttlSecondsAfterEmpty to 600 for GPUs in staging; 2) enable a small warm pool (2-4 nodes per AZ) for critical GPU queues; 3) split provisioners per-AZ to reduce cross-AZ contention for ENIs; 4) add a short provisioning backoff on ENI errors.
Shiv K: Also suggest turning off consolidation during high churn tests. We should test full flow with canary consolidation disabled and warm pool set.
Matt P: Cost tradeoff? Warm pools + per-AZ capacity will increase baseline cost. Rough calc: warm pool 3 nodes x 3 AZs x p4d = ~3 * 3 * $30/hr = $270/hr baseline; vs current on-demand churn cost which we estimate ~ $300-360/hr spurts. But it reduces failed launches and retries (operational cost).
Dmitri V: For dedicated GPU workloads we already get better utilization when we avoid repeated cold starts. My quick sim shows 8–12% uplift in steady-state infra cost but 40% fewer failed pod retries in the synthetic workload. Worth it for reliability.
Janet C: Proposed immediate plan for prod migration window: - ramp TTL to 600 and disable consolidation night-of for 48h (Janet -> will apply) - enable warm pool size=2 in each AZ (Shiv -> run canary) - create per-AZ provisioner draft and smoke (Olivia + Matt) - add simple ENI backoff in Karpenter config to avoid hot retry loops (Dmitri)
Matt P: I'll own the per-AZ provisioner PR. I'll also add a readiness gate that waits for cloud-init metadata before marking node ready. That should mitigate label drift.
Olivia S: I'll run canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC, will post results summary.
infra-bot: Scheduled: canary-gpu-warm-pool @ 2026-03-19T03:00:00Z by Olivia S.
Janet C: Thanks — if canary looks good we'll push the TTL + warm pool changes to prod during the migration window Fri 03:00->07:00 UTC. Any objections?
Shiv K: No objections. One extra ask: add a metric for "node_provision_error{reason=eni_exhaustion}" to the Karpenter dashboard so we can alert before client-visible failures.
Dmitri V: I'll add that metric and a 5m alert.
Janet C: Perfect. I'll update the migration runbook with owners and rollback: rollback = revert to autoscaler+node-pools for GPU groups. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
